rfi.description: A statue honouring Tiphaine Véron, the French tourist who vanished in Japan in 2018, was unveiled on Wednesday near the hotel where she was last seen. france24fr.description: Donald Trump a déclaré jeudi que son Conseil de la paix était parvenu à un accord pour le désarmement complet des combattants du Hamas et d'autres groupes armés dans la bande de Gaza, revendiquant une "étape monumentale" dans la mise en œuvre de son plan de paix pour l'enclave palestinienne. Le président américain a également affirmé qu'Israël quitterait la bande de Gaza une fois le Hamas désarmé.

france24fr.title: Ukraine : Zelensky accuse la Corée du Nord d'avoir fourni le missile ayant décimé une famille
france24fr.description: Après les attaques meurtrières de la nuit de mercredi à jeudi en Ukraine, le président Volodymyr Zelensky a accusé la Corée du Nord d'avoir fourni le missile balistique ayant anéanti une famille entière près de Kryvyï Rig, dans la région de Dnipropetrovsk.

france24fr.title: Incendies : accalmie espérée en France et en Espagne, de nouveaux feux de forêt gagnent l'Europe
france24fr.description: La France et l'Espagne entrevoient jeudi une accalmie après certains des incendies les plus violents de leur histoire récente, qui ont contraint des centaines de milliers de personnes à évacuer. Mais ailleurs en Europe, de nouveaux feux ravagent plusieurs régions, notamment en Grèce, au Royaume-Uni, au Portugal et en Turquie.

france24fr.title: 🔴 "Urgence humanitaire" à Ceuta après l'arrivée massive de migrants, l'armée envoyée en renfort
Le Bénin installe officiellement le Sénat, une nouvelle chambre du Parlement
france24fr.description: Le Bénin a officiellement installé son Sénat, nouvelle chambre du Parlement issue de la révision constitutionnelle de 2025, ce jeudi. La cérémonie a été marquée par la présence côte à côte des anciens présidents Patrice Talon et Boni Yayi. Cette nouvelle institutions a pour mission de réguler la vie politique dans le pays.

france24fr.title: Mali : 35 ans après la conférence nationale, où en est le pays ?
france24fr.description: Le 29 juillet 1991, le Mali ouvrait sa Conférence nationale après des décennies de dictature sous Moussa Traoré. Une constitution, un multipartisme et une promesse démocratique saluée dans tout le continent. 35 ans plus tard, les partis politiques sont dissous et les opposants emprisonnés. Que reste-t-il de cet héritage ?

france24fr.title: "Urgence humanitaire" à Ceuta après l'arrivée massive de migrants, l'armée envoyée en renfort
france24fr.description: Plusieurs centaines de personnes sont entrées illégalement jeudi dans l'enclave espagnole de Ceuta depuis le Maroc, neuf ont trouvé la mort durant la traversée. Alors que le ‌ministère de l'Intérieur a annoncé l'envoi de 60 soldats pour renforcer les forces ⁠de sécurité locales, des centaines de personnes étaient encore attendues à Fnideq, dans le nord du Maroc.

france24fr.title: Ceuta : une foule de migrants franchit la frontière entre le Maroc et l'Espagne
france24fr.description: Des milliers de migrants sont entrés jeudi dans l'enclave espagnole de Ceuta, ​en Afrique du Nord, débordant les forces de l'ordre après avoir traversé à la nage et escaladé les clôtures. "Les centres d'accueil sont débordés et saturés" : le président de Ceuta, Juan Jesus Vivas, a exhorté le gouvernement espagnol à déclarer l'état d'urgence face à ces arrivées massives.

france24fr.title: La France n’a pas refusé de faire appel à un bombardier d’eau russe par russophobie
france24fr.description: Alors que la flotte de Canadairs française connaît des problèmes d’indisponibilité, de nombreux internautes affirment qu’Emmanuel Macron aurait refusé d’employer un bombardier d’eau russe, le Beriev Be-200, pour des raisons idéologiques. C’est inexact : l'appareil a été rejeté car il ne correspondait pas aux besoins de la Sécurité civile.

france24fr.title: Frappes américano-saoudiennes : pourquoi Riyad déterre (un peu) la hache de guerre contre l'Iran
france24fr.description: Les frappes conjointes américano-saoudiennes en Irak, mercredi, représentent la première opération militaire à laquelle l’Arabie saoudite participe avec Washington depuis le début de la guerre contre l’Iran. Une étape dangereuse vient-elle d’être franchie ?

france24fr.title: Les sœurs Chawinga portent le Malawi, équipe surprise de la CAN féminine
france24fr.description: Lors de la Coupe d'Afrique des nations féminine au Maroc, deux sœurs qui jouent ensemble dans la sélection du Malawi ont attiré tous les regards. Temwa et Tabitha Chawinga ont brillé mardi lorsque leur équipe a battu à la surprise générale le Nigeria, tenant du titre.

france24fr.title: 🔴 L'UEFA vote à "l'unanimité" le boycott du Mondial face au projet d'investisseurs de la Fifa
"Il s'agit à 100 % d'un mammouth" : des ossements révélés par la décrue du Danube en Bulgarie
france24fr.description: Des ossements de mammouth ont été découverts en Bulgarie dans le lit du Danube, dont le niveau exceptionnellement bas pourrait mettre au jour d'autres vestiges, a déclaré jeudi à l'AFP le directeur du Musée régional d'histoire de Roussé, dans le nord du pays.

france24fr.title: L'UEFA vote à "l'unanimité" le boycott du Mondial face au projet d'investisseurs de la Fifa
france24fr.description: Les membres de l'UEFA ont voté à "l'unanimité" en faveur d'un boycott des prochaines Coupes du monde, en réaction au projet de la Fifa et de son président Gianni Infantino de céder une part de la compétition à des investisseurs privés, a annoncé jeudi l'instance européenne.

france24fr.title: "Pas d'atteinte à la liberté d'expression" : Nuñez répond à la polémique Xenia Fedorova
france24fr.description: L'arrêté d'expulsion visant la chroniqueuse prorusse Xenia Fedorova, accusée d'être la voix du Kremlin dans des médias français, n'est "pas une atteinte à la liberté d'expression", a affirmé jeudi le ministre de l'Intérieur français Laurent Nuñez. Une partie du Rassemblement national a salué la lutte contre l'ingérence russe tout en dénonçant un "deux poids deux mesures", d'autres élus et figures du camp ont eux dénoncé une censure politique.

Umsonst & Draußen: Seit 50 Jahren kostenlos - wie das dem Bardentreffen gelingt
Bulgarien: Dürre legt Mammutknochen im Flussbett der Donau frei

Popstar mit neuem Album: Ariana Grande und die Schattenseiten des Ruhms

zeit.title: Kevin Kühnert: »Das habe ich mir in den Politikjahren versaut«
zeit.description: Im Wochenendpodcast erklärt Kevin Kühnert, warum er »Podcast-Suchti« geworden ist. Und welche Spuren die Jahre in der Politik bei ihm hinterlassen haben.

zeit.title: Wahlausschüsse in Niedersachsen: Wer darf AfD-Politiker von der Wahl ausschließen?
zeit.description: Bei der Kommunalwahl in Niedersachsen dürfen mehrere AfD-Kandidaten nicht zur Wahl antreten. Gut für die Demokratie? Und: Wie verändert die Kakerlaken-Bewegung Indien?

OpenAI: Ist die KI außer Kontrolle?

spiegel.title: Kaufberatung für das erste eigene Auto: Wie Fahranfänger einen guten Gebrauchtwagen finden
spiegel.description: Junge Leute fahren oft ältere Autos – und weniger sichere. Das begrenzte Budget erzwingt Kompromisse. Doch wo sollte man die Grenze ziehen? Was Fahranfänger wissen müssen, was Experten raten.

spiegel.title: Waldbrände bei Bordeaux: Wie Saumos und Le Porge das Inferno erlebten
spiegel.description: Das Feuer begann in Saumos. Dann raste es durch Kiefernwälder in den Nachbarort Le Porge, den es großflächig zerstörte. Drei Anwohner erzählen, wie sie das Inferno erlebten.

spiegel.title: »The Invite«: Ist Heteros noch zu helfen? - Kritik
News: Verbraucher, Recht auf Repatarur, Deutscher Bundestag, Frauen-Ausgabe der Tour de France
spiegel.description: Verbraucher bekommen neue Rechte. Das Phantom des Deutschen Bundestags erklärt sich. Und die Frauen-Ausgabe der Tour de France startet. Das ist die Lage am Freitagmorgen.

spiegel.title: Ozempic-Abnehmspritze: Dieses Restaurant hat eine spezielle Speisekarte
spiegel.description: Wer die Abnehmspritze nimmt, verliert den Appetit, nicht die Lust aufs Essengehen. Ein Restaurant in Washington serviert nun spezielle Gerichte. Ich habe es ausprobiert.

spiegel.title: New York: Mutter und Großmutter ließen laut Anklage autistischen Teenager verhungern
spiegel.description: Der 16-Jährige kam mit massivem Untergewicht ins Krankenhaus – doch die Ärzte konnten nicht mehr helfen: In New York ist ein Teenager verhungert. Nun gibt es schwere Anschuldigungen gegen engste Verwandte.

spiegel.title: Auch KI von Anthropic griff echte Firmen an
spiegel.description: Dass ein KI-Modell von OpenAI auf eigene Faust zum Hacker wurde, galt als »beispielloser Zwischenfall« und Weckruf für die Techbranche. Nun stellt sich heraus: Es war kein Einzelfall.

spiegel.title: Apple verkündet Rekordzahlen – Aktienkurs bricht ein
spiegel.description: Das vergangene Quartal für Apple lief außerordentlich gut: Umsätze und Gewinn stiegen deutlich. Analysten zeigten sich trotzdem enttäuscht: Sie halten den Boom der vergangenen Monate für ein Strohfeuer.

spiegel.title: Javier Milei: Argentiniens Präsident will Ausländer rauswerfen, die »Hassbotschaften« verbreiten
spiegel.description: Javier Milei neigt zu rüpelhaften Auftritten, das bewies er zuletzt mit einem Eklat in Brasilien. Da ist es umso bemerkenswerter, wie hart der argentinische Präsident nun gegen Ausländer vorgehen will – und mit welcher Begründung.

spiegel.title: Donald Trump: US-Präsident könnte Todd Blanche als Justizminister vorerst zurückziehen
spiegel.description: Senatoren seiner eigenen Partei rebellieren. Deshalb erwägt der US-Präsident, Todd Blanche als Kandidaten für das Justizministerium zurückzuziehen – und auf Zeit zu spielen. Das wäre ein riskanter Schritt.

spiegel.title: Donald Trump verkündet Vereinbarung zur »vollständigen Entwaffnung« der Hamas
spiegel.description: Der US-Präsident spricht von einem »Meilenstein«: Laut Donald Trump will der sogenannte Friedensrat ausgehandelt haben, dass die Hamas in Gaza ihre Waffen abgibt. Die Miliz selbst hält sich bisher bedeckt.

spiegel.title: Migrationskrise: Zwei Theorien zum Grenzchaos von Ceuta
spiegel.description: Tausende Marokkaner erreichen die Stadt Ceuta, eine Exklave an der nordafrikanischen Küste. Der Andrang ist enorm – und besorgt die Anwohner. Zum Chaos an der Grenze kursieren zwei Theorien.

spiegel.title: Nach Uefa: Nächster Verband stellt sich gegen Fifa-Plan
spiegel.description: Gianni Infantino handelt sich mit seinen Plänen zum Teilverkauf der Fußball-WM weiter Kritik ein: Nach Boykottdrohungen der Uefa stellt sich nun auch der nord- und mittelamerikanische Verband Concacaf gegen ihn.

spiegel.title: Berlin: Wasserbüffel büxen aus und laufen durch Wohngebiet
spiegel.description: »Nervös, aber friedlich«: In Berlin tummelten sich heute früh Verkehrsteilnehmer auf den Straßen, die klar fehl am Platz waren – zehn Wasserbüffel waren aus ihrem Gehege entkommen. Die Polizei brachte sie wieder heim.

spiegel.title: Wetter: Deutscher Wetterdienst misst (vorläufig) Temperaturrekorde in drei Bundesländern
spiegel.description: In drei Bundesländern ist das Thermometer so hoch wie nie zuvor im Juli gestiegen, die Pegelstände in Rhein und Donau erreichen historische Tiefstände.

spiegel.title: Falsche Afrika-Karte präsentiert – US-Außenministerium zerknirscht
spiegel.description: Die Elfenbeinküste lag im Süden, Nigeria ohne Zugang zum Meer in der Mitte und Mosambik am Horn von Afrika: Das US-Außenministerium entschuldigt sich für die Verwendung einer falschen Afrika-Karte.

spiegel.title: Uefa-Boykott der Fifa-WM? Endlich spielen die Europäer ihre Stärke aus - Kommentar
spiegel.description: Der WM-Investorenplan von Fifa-Boss Infantino ist praktisch tot, dank des beherzten Eingreifens der Uefa. Die Argumente der Europäer sind nachvollziehbar, sie können sich aber schnell gegen sie selbst wenden.

spiegel.title: USA: Vater von Amokläufer zu 15 Jahren Haft verurteilt
spiegel.description: Sein Sohn hatte einen Schrein für einen Amokläufer aufgebaut: Trotzdem gab ein Vater in den USA ihm eine Waffe, mit der er vier Menschen tötete. Nun sind Vater und Sohn zu Haftstrafen verurteilt worden.

observador.title: O que pensa o Presidente sobre o caso Luís Neves?
observador.description: António José Seguro mantém-se em silêncio sobre o caso Luís Neves. Mas o que pensa o Presidente, o que tem feito e o que mais o preocupa em toda esta polémica?

observador.title: 4h. Exames. Reapreciações chegam a meio do prazo
observador.description: Período de correção começou na segunda e acaba dia 4 de agosto. Ainda, Pedro Sánchez visita esta sexta-feira Ceuta depois de milhares de pessoas terem tentado atravessar fronteira com Marrocos a nado.

observador.title: 3h. MAI. Seguro preocupado com desgaste das Instituições
observador.description: Presidente da República tem estado atento ao caso e prepara-se para falar. Ainda neste jornal, Montenegro diz que propostas da Air France/KLM e da Lufthansa valorizaram TAP acima do expectável.

observador.title: 2h. Diminuição do vento ajuda a combater fogo em Vinhais
observador.description: Casas já não estão em risco e pessoas retiradas de Vale das Fontes e de Rebordelo já regressam às habitações. Ainda, Passos Coelho diz que ninguém está despreocupado com polémicas em Portugal.

observador.title: 1h. Trump anuncia "acordo histórico" para desarmar Hamas
observador.description: Presidente norte-americano adianta que plano será aplicado de forma faseada e que prevê a retirada das forças israelitas do território. Ainda, Presidente da República preocupado com caso Luís Neves.

observador.description: Fontes governamentais explicaram à imprensa que só a “bolha” se interessa por “casos”. O “povo” não quer saber. Mas o “povo” cínico e indiferente não será, afinal, mais uma fantasia da “bolha”?

observador.title: O desaparecimento dos Pirilampos
observador.description: É o medo do declínio que nos está a atrair para o vazio. Como Pasolini, quanto mais apontamos para o desaparecimento, mais próximos estamos do fim.

observador.description: Burlas informáticas e furtos por carteiristas estão entre os crimes com maior aumento. Violência doméstica registou mais 217 processos do que em 2025.

observador.title: A justiça começa onde a previsão termina
observador.description: Quando as probabilidades substituem os factos e as previsões antecipam o julgamento, a tecnologia deixa de servir a justiça para começar a redefini-la.

observador.description: O Benfica está assim apurado para a 3ª pré-eliminatória de acesso à Liga Europa. Ainda, milhares de pessoas chegaram hoje a Ceuta a nado desde Marrocos. Pelo menos 18 morreram.

observador.title: A tentação do bem comum
observador.description: A tentação consequencialista, mascarada de “bem comum”, é tanto mais perigosa quanto mais convencidos estamos de que a nossa posição política de partida é moralmente correcta e superior.

observador.title: O mercado? O mercado é uma instituição
observador.description: Nunca a esquerda nacional entenderá que o mercado é uma instituição com regras próprias que o direito reconhece, organiza e afeiçoa mas que não pode ignorar, muito menos contrariar.

observador.title: Clima torna incêndios mais prováveis em Espanha
observador.description: Prevê-se que eventos destes ocorram uma vez a cada seis anos no centro de Espanha. Incêndios deslocaram cerca de 300 mil pessoas. Dizem ser impactos crescentes do aquecimento antropogénico.

observador.title: Lucro da Apple sobre 20% com recorde no 3º trimestre fiscal
observador.description: Receitas de 364 mil milhões de dólares e margens brutas acima de 50%. Trimestre de junho fica marcado pela última conferência de resultados de Tim Cook.

observador.description: Uma pergunta incómoda. Estamos a usar a inteligência artificial para desenvolver o homem? E outra: Estamos a treinar o homem para deixar de o ser?

undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

phys-org.title: Learning to better understand bone-like minerals
phys-org.description: A University of California San Diego research team has found a better way to understand and stabilize hydroxyapatite, the calcium phosphate mineral that makes up much of our teeth and bones. By adding tiny amounts of europium, a rare-earth element that mimics calcium, the team discovered a way to make the material potentially more useful for medical imaging.

phys-org.title: New report highlights health of the UK's plankton communities
phys-org.description: Researchers from the University of Plymouth have led the production of a new report highlighting the impact of climate change on marine plankton and pelagic habitats in U.K. waters. Published by the Marine Climate Change Impacts Partnership (MCCIP), the report discusses the latest evidence showing major large-scale shifts already happening in plankton communities.

phys-org.title: Probing binary stars in the Small Magellanic Cloud with the JWST
phys-org.description: The formation and evolution of individual stars in a galaxy shape the evolution of the galaxy itself. Stars and stellar remnants make up the vast majority of a galaxy's mass, so it's not surprising that the stellar population affects the evolution of galaxies. In the Milky Way's disk and bulge, stars and dead stars make up about 85% of the baryonic mass.

phys-org.title: Waste CO₂ converts into graphite through a newly observed two-step process
phys-org.description: Graphite, the carbon core of a humble No. 2 pencil, is also an essential component in technologies such as batteries, smartphones, laptops and industrial power equipment. Today, nearly all of this critical mineral must be mined and processed and, in the United States, imported.

phys-org.title: Survey highlights AI's potential to advance accessibility in work and learning
phys-org.description: As artificial intelligence becomes part of how people work, learn and solve problems, a new University of Phoenix survey conducted by The Harris Poll finds that recent working learners see meaningful opportunities for AI to support accessibility.

phys-org.title: Risks of debris between the Earth and the moon for future exploration
phys-org.description: Cislunar space has become the focal point of considerable interest and strategic planning because of the many proposed missions to send crews to the moon in the next decade. These include NASA's Artemis program, China and Russia's International Lunar Research Station (ILRS), the European Space Agency's Argonaut program and others. phys-org.title: Photonic time crystals unlock ultrafast control of light in the terahertz range
phys-org.description: An international team of researchers from École Polytechnique, Collège de France and Helmholtz-Zentrum Dresden-Rossendorf (HZDR) has achieved a world first: the experimental realization of an all-optical photonic time crystal (PTC), a material whose optical properties can be strongly and periodically modulated over ultrafast timescales.

phys-org.title: Bacteria build a mineral shield that could help marine infrastructure resist rust
phys-org.description: Researchers at Reichman University have developed a biological method for protecting marine infrastructure from corrosion caused by prolonged exposure to seawater. The study, published in Cell Reports Physical Science, presents an environmentally friendly alternative to the chemical corrosion inhibitors currently used to protect metals—materials that can be both polluting and costly.

phys-org.title: A thermal camera trick could let LIGO see twice as far
phys-org.description: There's a nice kind of irony buried in this story: One of the most sensitive instruments ever built, capable of measuring distortions smaller than the width of a proton, has been quietly held back by something as mundane as heat. And the fix, it turns out, is not some exotic new sensor but a thermal camera you could genuinely buy off the shelf.

phys-org.title: Pacific Ocean pattern helps explain diverging wildfire trends in US and Australia
phys-org.description: Two of the world's most fire-prone regions have followed strikingly different wildfire trajectories despite both experiencing a warming climate. Burned forest area has surged across the U.S. Southwest, while eastern Australia has not seen the same increase.

phys-org.title: Rural runoff funnels hurricane floodwater toward coastal cities, model finds
phys-org.description: Coastal cities are at increasing risk of compound flooding events, such as when heavy rainfall and storm surges occur simultaneously during hurricanes. However, the processes that contribute to urban compound flooding aren't well understood at smaller scales.

phys-org.title: Natural emulsion manages to stop fungus that threatens up to 80% of cocoa production
phys-org.description: An innovative formulation based on natural compounds could become a sustainable alternative for controlling moniliasis, one of the most devastating diseases affecting cocoa in Latin America. A new study shows that emulsions combining fengycin—a lipopeptide produced by bacteria of the genus Bacillus—with essential oils can significantly inhibit the growth of the fungus Moniliophthora roreri, responsible for losses that can exceed 70–80% of the harvest.

phys-org.title: Female birds have shorter lifespans than male birds across 35 North American species, researchers find
phys-org.description: Birds have a lot to do in their short lives: defend territories, build nests, raise chicks and feed themselves. But the toll of these activities may be greater for female birds than for male birds. A new study by UCLA ornithologists has found that female birds have lower survival rates than males. The research is the first to study female bird survival in a large dataset and shows that the phenomenon is more widespread than previously recognized. phys-org.title: How an embryo draws the line between body and germline
phys-org.description: Every embryo of an organism that reproduces sexually faces an early and consequential decision: which of its cell lineages will make up the mortal body, and which will become the germline, the lineage that eventually makes eggs or sperm and carries genetic information to the next generation. Get this wrong, and an organism can live but cannot reproduce and, evolutionarily, ceases to exist.

phys-org.title: Bacteria may identify a virus without recognizing its DNA
phys-org.description: When a virus enters a cell, its top priority is to replicate its genome rapidly, creating new viruses to infect elsewhere. The host has the opposite priority: to destroy the virus, ideally before it can do any harm. Biology has evolved diverse tactics for viral recognition and destruction, but they share a common theme—sensing that an invading viral genome is present in a cell.

phys-org.title: Scientists have found a new way molecules can cooperate at room temperature
phys-org.description: What if glowing molecules could synchronize, much like fireflies flashing in unison? phys-org.title: Turkey confronts growing wildfires on tourist coasts
phys-org.description: Hundreds of Turkish firefighters on Thursday battled to contain wildfires spreading near key tourist regions on the country's Mediterranean coast.

phys-org.title: Uncovering the structure of the poxvirus 'portal complex'
phys-org.description: Poxviruses have a long history in human disease as well as medicine: The first-ever vaccine was developed to protect against smallpox, which has since been eradicated. Despite this, scientists still don't fully understand how poxviruses infect and replicate inside our cells. Recent outbreaks of mpox highlight an urgent need to better understand poxvirus biology.

proj-syn.title: The Limits of Asia’s Two Major Growth Models
proj-syn.description: Data from a period in which both China and India pursued deliberate industrial policies show that neither country's development route is accessible to other countries. At best, their experience can alert policymakers to structural limitations and coordination problems that will require their own homegrown solutions.

proj-syn.title: The World Needs Compassionate AI
proj-syn.description: With AI having become the frontline of an intense global competition for economic and geopolitical power, speed is rewarded, scale is celebrated, and market dominance is prized above all else. Under such conditions, we risk forgetting the most important question: Whom is this intelligence ultimately meant to serve?

proj-syn.title: Trump’s New Tariffs Are an Opportunity to Fight Back

proj-syn.title: Explaining China’s Industrial Competitiveness
proj-syn.description: External headwinds have not weakened China’s manufacturing competitiveness. That is because the Chinese economy combines an unusually large manufacturing base, deep supply chains, fast engineering feedback loops, and cutthroat domestic competition to create global powerhouses.

proj-syn.title: When Politicians Ignore Economic Expertise
proj-syn.description: As politicians encroach on areas that require technical knowledge, the risk of costly policy mistakes increases. The failures of Narendra Modi and Donald Trump show that when it comes to economic policymaking, political acumen is no substitute for a deep understanding of incentives, markets, and institutions.

proj-syn.title: The Beijing Model Meets the Brussels Effect
proj-syn.description: As Europe races to rebuild its industrial base, China is focusing more on influencing international standards and governance frameworks. The two powers are converging because neither can hope to claim a dominant position in the global energy transition by relying wholly on its traditional strengths.

proj-syn.title: The Mexican Government’s Economic Spin
proj-syn.description: By cherry-picking 12 data points that supposedly contradict top ratings agencies’ assessment of Mexico’s economy and fiscal outlook, Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum recently presented a just-so story that should convince no one. A glimpse of what her list excludes makes that clear.

proj-syn.title: The Middle-Income Health Trap
proj-syn.description: Many countries that graduate from low- to middle-income status soon find themselves stuck in the position of being too rich to qualify for aid, too poor to secure reliable market-based financing, and too indebted to expand public-health spending. But it doesn't have to be this way.

proj-syn.title: Europe Is Fiddling While Rome Burns
proj-syn.description: Focusing only on emergency planning, disaster response, and recovery after each climate catastrophe is no longer enough in Europe. Policymakers urgently need to start mapping Europe’s long-term future, which will require a fundamental overhaul of its infrastructure, energy system, and major economic sectors.

proj-syn.title: Saving Democracy Requires Taxing Extreme Wealth
proj-syn.description: If lawmakers are serious about addressing the threat that dynastic wealth poses to American democracy, they can draw on considerable research that has gone into designing a wealth tax that avoids the pitfalls of other countries’ attempts. With the appearance of the world’s first trillionaire, there is no time to waste.

proj-syn.title: The AI Threat to Financial Stability
proj-syn.description: In episodes like the railroad boom and the dot-com bubble, creditors and shareholders were wiped out, because investment in a genuinely transformative technology outpaced any plausible near-term return. With the US financial system and asset markets having become a one-way bet on AI, such an outcome today could be catastrophic.

proj-syn.title: South Korea Bets on Industrial Policy Again
proj-syn.description: With industrial policy back in fashion worldwide, the question is not whether governments should intervene (they already do), but how they should proceed when they do not know in advance what will work. The answer lies in directed improvisation: creating the conditions for experimentation where it counts.

proj-syn.title: America Is Betting Against International Law
proj-syn.description: After cooperating with the International Criminal Court to indict Russian President Vladimir Putin for war crimes, the US has shifted to waging a scorched-earth campaign against the ICC in the name of protecting Israel. But rather than halting international law’s progress, the US is merely handing the pen to other countries.

proj-syn.title: The Therapist in Your Pocket
proj-syn.description: A new survey conducted by AXA and Ipsos shows that people are readily turning to AI chatbots to cope with mental-health problems. To ensure that these tools do more good than harm, health leaders, employers, insurers, and AI developers must take responsibility for steering them in a beneficial direction.

proj-syn.title: The Cost of Not Building Data Centers
proj-syn.description: In July, New York became the first state to enact a moratorium on new data centers, a path that other states may follow. But US policymakers, drawing lessons from past failures to make economy-wide investments in electrification and rare-earth processing, should weigh the strategic costs of not building essential infrastructure.

proj-syn.title: The Dangerous Spread of Jim Crow Nostalgia
proj-syn.description: With inaccurate claims about Black Americans’ poverty and crime rates having migrated from the far-right fringe to mainstream outlets like the Wall Street Journal, it is worth considering what the data actually say. Doing so will show that there is no empirical basis for such claims, only an ideological one.
